desc: Parse input: read N, K and the array A from stdin using fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer).
Build frequency array freq[v] for v up to M = max(A), then compute cnt[d] = sum of freq over multiples of d (sieve loop, O(M log M)).
Compute best[v]: iterate d from M down to 1; if cnt[d] >= K, assign best[m] = d for all multiples m of d that are not yet set (descending order guarantees the first assignment is the maximum).
Handle edge cases: K = 1 (answer is A_i itself, which the general logic already yields since cnt[A_i] >= 1) and values with no qualifying divisor other than 1.
Produce output: for each i in order, write best[A_i] on its own line, using a single joined string write for speed.
Verify correctness against the provided samples mentally and check complexity/memory fit (arrays of size ~1e6+1 of ints).

Implement the full solve() in Python with array('I') for memory safety, slice-sum for cnt, descending-d marking with early termination for best, and joined-string output; verify against samples and edge cases.
